semantics.evaluation: first-match-wins over `rules`, then `default`. '*' matches any value.

verdicts.allow+log: permitted; the executing tool MUST append a ledger line (JSONL: ts, corpus, provider, purpose, path, tool)
verdicts.conditional: permitted ONLY when the rule's `condition` holds; otherwise treat as deny
verdicts.pending-operator: evaluates as DENY. A named operator decision is required to flip this cell; flipping it is a one-line PR on this file

semantics.note: embedding, rerank, and vision-embedding send FULL content (text or images) to the provider — they are content egress, not metadata egress.

corpora.salus: any path under a `.salus`-marked root, or under a root listed in ~/.config/claude-glm/phi-roots or ~/.config/claude-glm/egress-denylist (the shared glm-guard.ts / parity_guard.py primitives)
corpora.luna-personal: the luna vault root EXCLUDING Clippings/ (journals, maps, sessions, notes)
corpora.handover-state: the handover state repo root (HANDOVER_DIR; work artifacts, specs, session notes). Kept for Mode-B EXTERNAL state repos after the HIMMEL-343 fold: a HANDOVER_DIR nested INSIDE a vault classifies as that vault's corpus instead (fence precedence checks vault roots first — more restrictive; pinned by test, HIMMEL-817)
corpora.himmel-code: himmel checkout(s), worktrees, and the public mirror (code + docs; public-propagated)
corpora.voice-audio: CAPTURED AUDIO: microphone recordings and any audio file derived from them (reference clips, TTS output). UNLIKE every other corpus this one is NOT path-keyed — speech has no file location, so it cannot be scoped by directory and the path-keyed salus deny cannot reach it (HIMMEL-1522). SCOPE NOTE: an utterance the operator DELIBERATELY addressed to the assistant (wake-word gated, or an explicit push-to-talk take) becomes an ordinary prompt once transcribed, governed by the same rules as typed input — it is not held here. The hazard this corpus exists for is AMBIENT audio: sound captured without the speaker addressing the system, which no path-keyed rule can protect. An earlier draft held transcripts here too, which forbade the product itself — a rule that outlaws its own use case is one that gets ignored, so the boundary is drawn at capture instead. Residual risk (unclosed, ticketed): a wake-gated utterance can still contain PHI, and nothing classifies it before it is sent
corpora.leg-failure-metadata: DERIVED leg-failure metadata (HIMMEL-4670 P5): class keys from closed vocabularies, counts, leg labels, ticket keys, PR numbers, hook or suite basenames and the fixed routing-table text that scripts/eval/leg-digest/failure_router.py builds from the leg-failures ledger. Never transcript content: no command, path, message or prompt (the ledger schema refuses those keys and the router's body alphabet check refuses anything else). NOT path-keyed: it exists only as the router-built Jira summary and body
corpora.mcp-tool-catalog: PUBLISHED MCP tool-catalog metadata (HIMMEL-4938): the tool names, descriptions and JSON schemas an MCP server returns for tools/list. Vendor-published text, identical for every caller; no ticket, vault, handover or corpus content is part of it. The request carries only the operator's own Atlassian credential for auth

ollama-cloud.note: HIMMEL-4185: Ollama's hosted models. graphify-fence.sh classifies `--backend ollama` as ollama-cloud when the model ends in -cloud or :cloud (the local daemon forwards those to ollama.com), or when OLLAMA_BASE_URL/OLLAMA_HOST points at ollama.com. HIMMEL-1522: the salus PHI deny keys on FILE PATHS, and speech has none — a mic streaming to a cloud API bypasses the PHI perimeter entirely, because there is no path for the guard to inspect. Audio cannot be classified before it is heard, so ALL captured audio is held at the salus tier. Flipping this needs a mechanism that can prove PHI is absent from speech BEFORE it is sent; no such mechanism exists, so no operator decision can be recorded here that opens it
